sources.headline: Hundreds arrested in anti-Trump protests in Philippines amid anger over Iran war and AI pact
sources.text: Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as the US president arrived in the city for a leaders’ summit.Organisers claimed as many as 10,000 people would be joining protests against Trump in the capital of the Philippines on Tuesday, where he is attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit. The crowds were expected to try to march to the summit site.Authorities have arrested nearly 300 people in widespread protests held in the days leading up to the summit, with large parts of the capital closed off and tight security in place.Some burned effigies of Trump and faced off with police officers armed with batons and shields. Slogans on placards called the American leader the world’s “No 1 terrorist” in protests held on Monday.Demonstrators angry at the cost of living and energy shock caused by the Iran war, and the new US-led Pax Silica initiative on AI and critical minerals, tried to reach the summit at the Philippine International Convention Center on Monday, but were blocked by police.Pax Silica has sparked tensions in the Philippines over plans to build a tech hub outside Manila that critics say will affect water and energy supplies, and displace members of the Ayta Indigenous community.Large sections of central Manila were closed to the public as part of the security cordon and public holidays put in place for the Asean summit.Protesters clashed with police in Manila. Photograph: Noel Celis/ReutersAfter departing from Fairbanks in Alaska, Trump emerged from Air Force One at Ninoy Aquino International airport at 5.54pm local time (0954 GMT), live video showed.Trump will meet with the leaders of Australia, Japan and India on Tuesday night before heading to Shenzhen in China on Wednesday. There he will attend the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit and hold trilateral talks with China’s president, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin of Russia.The backlash against Trump follows the ousting of the boss of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, and allegations members of the US administration, including the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, knew about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.Trump’s delegation was expected to include Elon Musk.Protesters smash an effigy of Donald Trump at Liwasang Bonifacio Plaza in Manila. Photograph: Hollie Adams/ReutersProtest leader Renato Reyes blamed the arrests in Manila on the heavy handed response of the government on the president, Ferdinand Marcos Jr, calling Monday the largest single day of police arrests since Marcos came to office in 2022.“It is really crazy that the Philippine government is rolling out the red carpet for someone who has been so flatly rejected by the American people,” Reyes said. “Trump started a war that devastated the global economy and pushed oil prices in the Philippines to historic highs. It has caused untold suffering on the Filipino people.“So, yes, Trump will have to pay for his crimes and he will have to be answerable, not just to the American people, but to the people of the world.”The Philippine national police said some officers were injured during confrontations with demonstrators opposed to the summit, including when objects were allegedly thrown at officers.Pax Silica will include a technology hub planned at New Clark City in Tarlac, about 100km from Manila.Indigenous communities and other groups protest in Manila on Monday. Photograph: Nathaniel Soriano/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockIntended to bolster western stocks of AI technology and reduce “excessive dependencies” on single source supply chains, including from China, Pax Silica will provide chips and critical minerals to 26 participating signatory governments.Amnesty International said demonstrations should not be forcibly or violently dispersed.“Reports of arrests during the protests demand immediate scrutiny,” Amnesty’s director for the Philippines, Ritz Lee Santos III, said. “Authorities must explain the specific grounds for each arrest and any continued detention. Anyone detained solely for peacefully exercising their rights must be released immediately.”

sources.headline: Donald Trump meets ‘longtime friend’ Imelda Marcos during Philippines visit
sources.text: Trump told Philippine President Marcos he knew his ‘parents very well’.US President Donald Trump reunited with longtime friend Imelda Marcos, the widow of an ousted dictator and mother of the incumbent Philippine president, Ferdinand Marcos Jr.Trump got to know the Philippine first couple while partying in New York decades ago.Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3ASEAN summit: Who’s attending and what’s at stake?list 2 of 3Trump departs for ASEAN on summit with Xi and Putinlist 3 of 3US President Trump arrives in Manila ahead of ASEAN summitend of listWednesday’s brief encounter happened at Manila’s Malacanang presidential palace, where Trump was received with a red-carpet welcome and full military honours.On Tuesday evening, before a speech to Asian leaders, Trump praised Marcos and his parents, saying, “I just don’t wanna date myself, but I knew your parents very well,” adding that Marcos Jr had “good genetics”.Imelda Marcos now 97, was known for her lavish lifestyle and vast collection of expensive shoes accumulated while her husband, Ferdinand Marcos, was in power as president for more than 20 years, at a time when many Filipinos lived in poverty-stricken conditions.Since Marcos was ousted in the 1986 “people power” revolution, Imelda has faced several charges of embezzlement, corruption and tax evasion.Ferdinand Marcos Jr, right, with his mother, former first lady Imelda Marcos, in Manila, Philippines, on June 30, 2022 [File: Ezra Acayan/Getty Images]Once seated inside the sprawling palace for their meeting, Trump told Marcos their countries’ people have a lot in common and stressed “architectural tastes”.“I love what you’ve done here,” Trump said, referring to the palace. “You’ve done a fantastic job.”Marcos said he sent Trump a delivery from Jollibee, the Philippines’ biggest homegrown fast-food chain, so he could have a “taste of Manila” during his short stay in the capital.Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday night to join leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) at their annual summit meetings.On Wednesday, Trump shook hands and exchanged greetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin before a group photo at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China.

sources.headline: Fried chicken and a chat with an old friend: How Marcos catered to Trump
sources.text: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines flattered President Trump during his brief visit to Manila. It is unclear what dividends the strategy will yield.
